It sounds like you’re trying to figure out whether your car’s current gas supply will carry you across the ~750 mi stretch between Rivermist and Stonebrook. To give you a solid estimate, it would help to know:

| Piece of info | Why it matters |
|---------------|----------------|
| Current fuel level (in gallons or percent full) | Determines how much energy you actually have left |
| Fuel tank size / maximum capacity | Lets us calculate the *maximum* range possible |
| Vehicle’s average fuel economy (mpg or L/100km) | Needed to translate “fuel” into “miles” |

If you can share those three bits—especially the fuel level and mpg—I’ll crunch the numbers for you right away. In the meantime, here’s a quick sanity check formula you can run yourself:

```
Remaining Range ≈ (Gallons Left ÷ Miles per Gallon) × 1 mile
```

For example, if you’ve got 10 gal left and your car averages 25 mpg, you’d expect around 250 mi of usable range before needing another refill.

Let me know the specifics when you can, and I’ll confirm whether you’ll hit the highway safely—or if you’ll need to plan a pit stop along the way.
